title: Hugging Face releases four NVIDIA Cosmos 3 open-weight checkpoints
excerpt: The new 16B parameter models are designed for interactive world simulation and multi-sensor driving scene generation.
bodyHtml:
Hugging Face announced on November 5, 2026, that the NVIDIA Cosmos world model development platform has added four new open-weight checkpoints to its Cosmos 3 model family. These models, which feature 16B trainable parameters, are intended for generating interactive world simulations and multi-sensor, multi-view driving scenes.

The new checkpoints include Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto for generating multi-view driving data, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto for streaming camera and LiDAR observations, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer for rendering photorealistic video from simulator controls, and Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual for predicting video from robot actions. All four models are post-trained examples of Cosmos 3 Nano and are released under the OpenMDW1.1 license, which permits commercial and non-commercial use.

The models utilize a Mixture-of-Transformers backbone that connects text-processing and visual-generation networks through attention. Developers can adapt these models using a four-stage training recipe that includes bidirectional adaptation, teacher forcing, consistency distillation, and self-forcing. The checkpoints are available for download alongside a technical report and demonstration videos.
